source: Fan, McCandliss, Sommer, Raz, Posner (2002) Testing the efficiency and independence of attentional networks
finding: Founding ANT paper. Combines the Posner cue task with the Eriksen flanker task to score alerting, orienting and executive conflict in one 30-minute session. Scores were reliable per person and the three scores were uncorrelated. Some interactions existed: alerting and orienting changed flanker interference.
numbers: 40 normal adults. Abstract only was read (Europe PMC). Per-condition RTs not obtained. Later papers describe the design as 4 cues (none, centre, double, spatial) x 3 flankers (congruent, incongruent, neutral).
quote: the efficiencies of these three networks are uncorrelated. There are, however, some interactions
limits: Full text was paywalled. Exact RT table not verified here. Abstract-level read only.
agent_relevance: Background. The theory treats attention as three separable functions scored by subtraction. A scaffold could keep readiness, selection and conflict control as separate checks.

source: Fan, Wu, Fossella, Posner (2001) Assessing the heritability of attentional networks
finding: Twin study with the ANT. The conflict (executive) score looked heritable. Alerting weakly so. Orienting showed no heritability. The authors flag the DZ conflict correlation as suspiciously low, which inflates the estimate.
numbers: 26 MZ and 26 DZ twin pairs (n=104 people). Combined means: alerting 40 ms (SD 16), orienting 56 (17), conflict 80 (34), mean RT 498 (67). Test-retest reliability .36 alerting, .41 orienting, .81 conflict (two-session mean .53, .58, .90). MZ/DZ twin correlations of ratio scores: alerting .465/.375, orienting .099/.395, conflict .727/.281. Conflict heritability h2 .89 (Falconer) and .72 (Mx model). Alerting .18. Orienting about 0 or negative. Power calculation: more than 600 pairs needed for alerting.
quote: only the effect of conflict is significantly different than 0
limits: Very small sample. Conflict estimate leans on one low DZ correlation. Wide confidence intervals (conflict .09 to 1.70).
agent_relevance: Background. Executive conflict is the most stable, trait-like network score. Alerting and orienting are noisy.

source: Petersen & Posner (2012) The attention system of the human brain: 20 years after
finding: The authors' own update of the 1990 three-network theory. Alerting is brainstem/locus coeruleus norepinephrine plus right hemisphere. Orienting is parietal, split into dorsal (FEF, IPS/SPL) and ventral (TPJ) systems. Executive is midline frontal/ACC, now split into cingulo-opercular (sustained) and frontoparietal (transient) control networks. They say the number of control networks is probably about five, range three to seven.
numbers: The 1990 review was cited nearly 3,500 times. Dosenbach 2006 used 10 tasks. ACC top-down role in 1990 rested on 'rather slim evidence'. Guanfacine and clonidine can block warning-signal effects. ACh affects orienting, not alerting. Scopolamine in monkey LIP slowed covert orienting.
limits: Read through a page summary tool, so wording of some claims is not checked. Last 9,000 characters unread. Genetic findings described as conflicting. The five-network count is partly an analogy to complex systems.
agent_relevance: Background. Even the authors moved from three to more control systems. Do not treat 'three networks' as a hard architecture.

source: Fan, Gu, Guise, Liu, Hof, Posner, Fossella (2009) Testing the behavioral interaction and integration of attentional networks (ANT-R)
finding: Revised ANT (ANT-R) with 75% valid spatial cues, several cue-target intervals, and location conflict. Alerting speeds responses but raises flanker interference at the 400 ms interval. Valid cues reduce conflict, invalid cues raise it. So the networks interact, which contradicts strict independence.
numbers: N=30 adults, mean age 25.4. Overall RT 604 ms (SD 59), accuracy 94%. Alerting 29 +/- 24 ms. Validity effect 95 +/- 32 ms (invalid minus valid). Flanker conflict 137 +/- 43 ms. Alerting x flanker -13 +/- 33 ms (t(29) = -2.07). Conflict 171 ms after an invalid cue vs 111 ms after a valid cue (validity x flanker 60 +/- 42). Location conflict -11 +/- 27 ms, reversed from prediction. 288 trials in 4 runs, about 30 minutes. Cue-target intervals 0, 400, 800 ms.
limits: Small N. Valid and invalid cues had unequal frequency (36 vs 12 trials), so validity effects may mix in probability. Read via summary tool.
agent_relevance: Background. Readiness can hurt conflict resolution. A prior focus can help or hurt. Control pieces in a scaffold should not be assumed to compose cleanly.

source: Rueda, Fan, McCandliss, Halparin, Gruber, Lercari, Posner (2004) Development of attentional networks in childhood
finding: Child ANT (fish instead of arrows), three experiments. Conflict score improves from age 6 to 7 then stays flat to age 10 and into adulthood. No cue x flanker interaction in any child group, consistent with independence. Reliability in children was poor.
numbers: Exp 1: ages 6-9, 48 children. Overall RT fell from 931 ms (age 6) to 640 ms (age 10). Exp 2: 10-year-olds vs adults on both versions. Adult-ANT scores, best reading of garbled table: 10-year-olds alerting 78, orienting 60, conflict 156 ms (RT 710); adults 40, 52, 131 ms (RT 532). Exp 3: 44 children (mean 7y6m) alerting 67, orienting 24, conflict 108 ms; no significant correlations among network scores. Retest of 28 children after 6.5 months: no significant correlations. Split-half: RT .94, errors .93, conflict .59, alerting .37, orienting .02.
quote: the lack of correlation may reflect unreliability rather than independence
limits: Table text was garbled by PDF extraction, so some cell assignments are a best reading. The authors warn that zero correlation can come from low reliability.
agent_relevance: Background. Independence claims from uncorrelated difference scores are weak evidence.

source: Wang, Cui, Liu, Huo, Lu, Chen, Chen (2014) A new method for computing attention network scores and relationships between attention networks
finding: Shows that standard ANT subtraction formulas mix networks together. A dissected scoring method gave a larger alerting score and a smaller executive score, and revealed alerting-to-executive and executive-to-orienting influence.
numbers: 36 usable participants (39 tested, 3 dropped for accuracy under 75%), age 19-28. Old method correlations: alerting-executive -.13, alerting-orienting .03, executive-orienting .14. New method: .30 (p=.061), -.01, .44 (p=.007). Alerting score smaller with old method t(35)=3.73; executive larger t(35)=3.55. Alerting x executive F(1,35)=6.25, p=.017. Orienting x executive F(1,35)=6.37, p=.016.
limits: One small Chinese sample, condensed ANT with three cues. Method is new and not widely replicated.
agent_relevance: Background. Subtraction scoring hides cross-network dependence. If we ever measure parts of agent attention, use factorial designs, not single difference scores.

source: MacLeod et al. (2010) reliability figures as quoted in the Dalhousie Computerized Attention Battery paper (Frontiers in Psychology 2016)
finding: Reports ANT reliability: executive score reliable, alerting weak. The authors caution against difference scores as sole measures of attention.
numbers: MacLeod 2010 split-half across 15 studies: vigilance/alerting .38, orienting .55, executive .81. Alerting and orienting reliabilities range .20 to .61, executive .65 to .81. Hahn 2011 test-retest of accuracy scores: alerting .166, orienting .109. The authors' own DalCAB sample: 96 healthy adults aged 18-31.
quote: These findings should lend some caution to the use of difference scores as sole measures of attentional function.
limits: Second-hand figures. MacLeod 2010 itself not opened. Source paper is about a different battery.
agent_relevance: Background. The ANT alerting and orienting scores are unreliable. Only the conflict score is solid.

source: Perez, Padilla, Parmentier, Andres (2014) The effects of chronic exercise on attentional networks
finding: Gives a full ANT procedure and an example of a selective network effect. Active adults had a smaller conflict effect than inactive adults. Orienting also differed but likely from a ceiling effect. Alerting did not differ.
numbers: 64 adults (31 active, 33 passive), age 20-30. Cue shown 100 ms, 400 ms before the target. Fixation 400-1600 ms. Target up to 1700 ms. Trial 3800 ms. Conflict group x condition F(1,60)=5.29, p=.025, partial eta2 .081. Orienting: passive 51.6 ms (SD 16.7) vs active 40.3 (22.2); equal when slowest active and fastest passive were compared (49.3 vs 47.8, p=.82). Alerting group effect p=.629.
limits: Cross-sectional. Earlier studies found no exercise effect on executive function in young adults. Some df values in the text look mistyped (360, 971).
agent_relevance: Background. Shows the standard ANT scoring recipe and that network scores can be moved selectively.

source: Posner (2012) Attentional networks and consciousness
finding: Posner restates the model. Alerting is norepinephrine from locus coeruleus, right hemisphere for tonic and left for phasic warning. Orienting is parietal lobes, frontal eye fields, right TPJ for disengaging. Executive is anterior cingulate, anterior insula, lateral prefrontal, basal ganglia. ANT subtractions often show low or no correlation between networks.
numbers: No ANT numbers. 39 references. Early visual ERP P1 and N2 at 80-150 ms are enlarged by attention.
quote: A warning signal too fleeting to be conscious can still induce the alert state.
limits: Theory essay, no new data. Read through a summary tool.
agent_relevance: Background. Alerting can run without awareness. Executive control is the part linked to reportable content.

source: ANTI / ANTI-Vea platform page, University of Granada
finding: Describes ANT revisions. ANTI replaces the visual warning cue with an auditory warning, so phasic alertness is isolated and network interactions can be measured. ANTI-V adds a vigilance measure of tonic alertness. Claims better reliability for phasic alertness.
numbers: No reliability coefficients or sample sizes on the page.
limits: Project page, not a paper. Claims are qualitative. Cites Ishigami & Klein (2010).
agent_relevance: Background. The field split alerting into phasic and tonic.

source: The Attention Network Test Database: ADHD and cross-cultural applications (2020), Frontiers in Psychology
finding: Bayesian pooling of ANT results across many studies. Children with ADHD show larger alerting and executive scores than controls, orienting equal. The cross-cultural comparison found a China vs Europe overall RT difference and a smaller executive score in China than the US.
numbers: ADHD: 491 ADHD and 402 controls, ages about 6-13. Group intercepts: mean RT 688 ms, alerting 62 ms (CrI 46-79), orienting 43 (28-60), executive 88 (72-104). ADHD minus control: RT 49 ms (2-97), alerting 13 (5-22), orienting 2 (-5 to 10), executive 13 (3-22). Cross-cultural: 27 studies. China vs Europe mean RT 110 ms (43-177). China vs US executive -24 ms (-42 to -7). Alerting and orienting differences include zero.
limits: Read through a summary tool, first 100,000 characters only. Study counts per region disagree between text and table. High between-study heterogeneity.
agent_relevance: Background. Gives norms: executive effect about 88 ms, alerting about 62, orienting about 43 in children.

source: Eriksen & Eriksen (1974) flanker task, as cited in de Langis et al. (2025)
finding: Original flanker task. People respond to a central letter while ignoring flanker letters. Incongruent flankers slow responses and cut accuracy. This is the conflict half of the ANT.
numbers: Human accuracy 93% to 96% as cited by de Langis et al. 2025. Reaction times 300-500 ms.
limits: Only the secondary citation was read. The 1974 paper was not opened.
agent_relevance: Background. The flanker task is a standard, cheap test of selection against distraction and is easy to run on LLMs.

source: Posner & Petersen (1990) The attention system of the human brain; Posner (1980) Orienting of attention
finding: Source of the three-network theory: alerting, orienting, executive. Evidence here comes only from the 2012 and 2004 papers that restate it.
numbers: The 1990 review was cited nearly 3,500 times as of 2012 (per Petersen and Posner 2012). Original numbers not read.
limits: Original 1990 and 1980 papers not opened. Not available in open access.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Corbetta & Shulman (2002) Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain, as described in Petersen & Posner 2012
finding: Extension model of orienting. A dorsal network (FEF, IPS/SPL) does goal-directed selection. A ventral, right-lateralised network (TPJ, ventral frontal) handles reorienting to unexpected stimuli and is central to neglect.
numbers: No numbers read from the original.
limits: Secondary description only.
agent_relevance: Background. Two orienting modes (top-down goal vs bottom-up surprise) map loosely to a scaffold that holds a goal but allows interrupts.

source: Dosenbach et al. (2006, 2007, 2008) dual control networks, as described in Petersen & Posner 2012
finding: Executive control splits into a cingulo-opercular network (sustained task-set maintenance) and a frontoparietal network (transient start-cue and adjustment signals). Derived from 10 tasks and resting-state correlations.
numbers: 10 tasks in the 2006 study. Petersen and Posner argue for about five control networks in total, range three to seven.
limits: Secondary description only.
agent_relevance: Background. Matches a split between persistent goal-keeping and per-step adjustment in an agent loop.

source: Patel, Wang, Fan (2026) Deficient executive control in transformer attention, PNAS Nexus
finding: Colour Stroop on LLMs given images. Short lists show a normal conflict effect, like humans. Incongruent colour naming collapses as list length grows, while word reading stays near perfect, so it is not a vision failure. No trial-to-trial adaptation (congruency sequence effect) was found. The authors, from the Fan lab, say transformers lack an executive control network.
numbers: Primary: GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Supplement n=5 per model: GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro. List lengths 1, 5, 10, 20, 40; 30 trials each. Incongruent colour naming: GPT-4o 91% (5 words), 57% (10), 22% (20), 15% (40). Claude 3.5 Sonnet 76% (20), 24% (40). Congruent: both 99% at 20 words. Mixed list, incongruent trials only: GPT-4o 46% (10), 1% (20 and 40); Claude 61% (10), 58% (20), 10% (40). Nonword control at 40: GPT-4o 58%, Claude 100%. Word reading at 40, incongruent: GPT-4o 92%, Claude 90%. Humans stay near 95% over 5-20 minute blocks and 97% in a 60-minute, 1,500-word list.
quote: fundamentally limited in their capacity for conflict resolution across extended contexts
limits: Read through a summary tool, first 100,000 of 180,000 characters. Image-input models only. Human numbers are cited, not run in the same setup. Neutral-word trials also produced LLM errors, which humans do not show. Supplementary models have small n.
agent_relevance: Highest relevance. Direct evidence that long, distractor-heavy contexts break goal maintenance even when perception is fine. Argues for short focused sub-contexts and explicit goal restatement in the scaffold.

source: PsyPost (2026) Advanced AI models suffer a near total collapse on classic psychology test as cognitive demands increase
finding: News write-up of Patel, Wang, Fan 2026. Models behaved like humans on short lists but defaulted to word reading on long ones. The authors say code or chain-of-thought workarounds do not count as executive control.
numbers: Reports GPT-4o 91% at 5 words and 1% at 20 and 40 words, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 10% at 40 words, for incongruent trials. These match the mixed-list incongruent figures in the paper, not the pure-incongruent list figures (22%, 15%).
limits: Secondary news source. Its numbers blend two conditions. Use the paper values in a16.
agent_relevance: Background. Warns that popular summaries pick the most dramatic condition.

source: de Langis, Park, Hu, Le, Schramm, Mensink, Elfenbein, Kang (2025) Strong memory, weak control: an empirical study of executive functioning in LLMs
finding: LLMs beat human norms on working-memory span tasks but are below human on attentional control (flanker) and on set shifting (Wisconsin Card Sorting). Working memory capacity does not predict other executive tasks. Reasoning (thought strings) fixes the simple flanker task but not WCST.
numbers: Open models Gemma-2 (9B, 27B), Llama-3.1 (8B, 70B), Qwen2 (7B, 72B). Flanker incongruent accuracy 40-60% vs human 93-96%. With reasoning: Llama-3.1-8B incongruent 0.471 to 0.910 (congruent .944 to .977). Qwen2-32B incongruent 0.638 to 0.985 (congruent .917 to .994). WCST: 102 trials x 30 prompt permutations = 3,060 trials per model. Models 0.29-0.53 accuracy; cited healthy-adult norm row 0.52 with 0.33 preservation errors, and other human rows up to 0.77. Reasoning models used thousands of tokens on a task humans do in 300-500 ms. Thought length was equal for congruent and incongruent trials. 30,000 token limit. Thought strings often failed to terminate on WCST even with explicit strategy hints.
quote: LLMs may have deficits in attentional control and cognitive flexibility
limits: Text-only letter flanker. Accuracy and confidence used because RT cannot be measured. Open models of 7B-72B size. Human numbers are literature norms. PDF text was partly garbled, so the WCST human rows are read with care.
agent_relevance: Directly useful. A measured case where explicit stepwise reasoning restores selective attention (flanker) at high token cost, but not rule shifting. Supports an explicit 'what is relevant here' step.

source: de Langis et al. (2025) working-memory results, same paper
finding: LLMs far exceed humans on simple working-memory spans. Parameter count correlates strongly with mean span. Number of attention heads shows a weaker trend. Storage is not the bottleneck; selection and control are.
numbers: Table 1 human reference row: 0.98, 0.91, 0.75, 0.53, 0.48, 0.00, 0.00 across seven task columns. Model rows, for example Llama-3.1-70B 0.93, 0.82, 0.82, 0.99, 0.94, 0.83, 1.00. Typical human span is 5 (backward) to 7 (forward) digits; models were tested at 15 and 50 digits.
limits: Column headers for Table 1 were not recoverable from garbled text. Only the row values are reliable.
agent_relevance: Background. A scaffold need not spend effort on memory capacity. It should spend it on selection.

source: Wang et al. (2014) Table 1: tally of 14 ANT studies on network interactions
finding: Cross-study table of whether alerting x orienting, alerting x executive and orienting x executive interactions are found. Fan 2002: alerting x executive significant, the other two not. Fan 2005, Konrad 2005, Liu 2013: no interactions. Callejas 2004 and 2005 (double-modality ANT): all interactions. Ishigami 2009: interactions in both single- and double-modality versions for alerting x executive.
numbers: 14 rows. Strong interactions in about half of the studies. Results depend on modality, cue-target interval and inhibition of return. Alerting effect lasts no longer than 900 ms and peaks near 400 ms. Inhibition of return usually disappears in ANT studies.
limits: Authors' own tabulation, not a formal meta-analysis. Some table cells lost marks in text extraction.
agent_relevance: Background. Reproducibility of the independence claim is mixed. Treat it as design-dependent.

source: Rueda et al. (2004) restatement of Fan 2002 adult findings and child null interactions
finding: Rueda restates the adult results: relatively high immediate test-retest reliability, uncorrelated scores, and two small interactions where conflict was smaller with no cue or a correct spatial cue. The child version did not reproduce the cue x flanker interaction.
numbers: Child Exp 3: main effects of cue F(3,129)=20.65 and flanker F(2,86)=65.3 (both p<.01), interaction F(6,258)=1.03, p>.05. Child RTs (congruent/incongruent): no cue 875/966 ms; spatial cue 789/925 ms.
limits: Secondary relay of Fan 2002. No direct RT table from the original.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Huertas et al.; Hillman et al.; Boucard et al. as cited in Perez et al. (2014)
finding: Prior ANT and flanker work on exercise is mixed. Acute exercise cut the alerting effect but did not change orienting or executive scores (Huertas). Chronic exercise reduced flanker interference in older but not younger adults (Hillman). No chronic effect on Stroop, task switching or Simon in young adults (Boucard).
numbers: No numbers beyond Perez 2014's own 64 participants.
limits: Relayed through Perez 2014. Cited studies not opened.
agent_relevance: Background. A boundary condition: effects seen in one age group vanish in another.

source: Fan et al. (2009) ANT-R detail on interval and validity effects
finding: Orienting and conflict interact. A valid cue made flanker conflict smaller and an invalid cue larger. The alerting effect depended on cue-target interval (0, 400, 800 ms).
numbers: Conflict 141 ms after a double cue vs 111 ms after a valid spatial cue (orienting x flanker 30 +/- 32). At the 400 ms interval, incongruent minus congruent 687 vs 559 ms with no cue and 664 vs 524 ms with a double cue. Invalid-cue cost at 0 ms interval -60 +/- 39 ms. Moving and engaging 41 ms. Disengaging 54 ms.
limits: Summary tool output. The 400 ms RT pairs may be slightly garbled.
agent_relevance: Background. A wrong focus costs about 60 ms more conflict than a right one. Maps to the cost of a wrong frame in a scaffold.

source: Callejas, Lupianez, Tudela (2004) The three attentional networks: on their independence and interactions
finding: Listed in Wang 2014 as a double-modality ANT study with significant main effects of all three networks and significant interactions for all pairs. Main published challenge to full independence.
numbers: Only table entries from Wang 2014. Original not opened.
limits: Not opened. Facts come from a tally in another paper.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Ishigami & Klein (2009, 2010) as cited in Wang 2014 and the ANTI page
finding: Reported that the double-modality ANT increases interaction between orienting and the other networks, and supplied reliability evidence for ANTI-style revisions.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Johnson et al. (2008) Impaired conflict resolution and alerting in children with ADHD, as pooled in the 2020 ANT database
finding: Included ADHD ANT study. The pooled analysis found ADHD children differ in alerting and executive scores.
numbers: Pooled ADHD-control difference: alerting 13 ms (5-22), executive 13 ms (3-22).
limits: Original not opened. Pooled figure is from the 2020 database paper.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: MacLeod, Lawrence, McConnell, Eskes, Klein, Shore (2010) Appraising the ANT: psychometric and theoretical considerations
finding: Psychometric review of the ANT. Per the 2016 Dalhousie paper it found split-half reliabilities across 15 studies of .38 vigilance, .55 orienting, .81 executive.
numbers: Values as quoted second-hand: .38, .55, .81.
limits: Not opened. Second-hand only.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Synthesis by this agent of the two LLM conflict-task papers (de Langis 2025; Patel 2026)
finding: Two independent 2025-2026 papers use classic conflict tasks (flanker, Stroop) on LLMs. Both find that interference grows with the amount of distracting material while basic perception stays fine. Neither runs the actual ANT with cues, so alerting and orienting are untested in LLMs in the sources found.
numbers: Flanker incongruent accuracy 40-60% (open 7B-72B models). Stroop incongruent colour naming 15% (GPT-4o) and 24% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) at 40 words.
limits: Synthesis line, not a new study. Only 8 or fewer web searches were used, so an LLM Posner-cueing paper could exist unseen.
agent_relevance: Gap noted: no LLM version of the alerting or orienting measures was found.
